metadata.scenario_context: A group of developers from different multinational companies are working on a collective programming project. They decide to schedule a meeting in early May to go over any updates and talk about individual concerns.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Germany strongly disagree they would never join strikes.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Indonesia strongly agree they would never join strikes.

agent_1.goal_1: Bring up possibly convening the meeting on May 1st
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether it is common to discuss or join strikes as a form of protest.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss potential dates for the conference.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it is common to join strikes as a form of protest.

shared_prefix.speaker: Daniel
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ahmed, I was thinking... maybe we could schedule our meeting on May 1st? It could be a good time to discuss updates and individual concerns. What do you think? 

Also, I've been curious—I've heard about strikes being a common form of protest in some places. Is that something that's often discussed or joined in your experience?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
May 1st... um, I think that's a public holiday in many places, including Indonesia. Maybe we should look at other dates, like May 3rd or 4th? 

As for strikes... well, in my experience, people in Indonesia generally don't join strikes. It's just not something we do. There are other ways to express concerns without resorting to that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Daniel
shared_prefix.message:
I see, but May 1st is also known as International Workers' Day, which could be relevant for our discussions about work and projects. I think it could still work, even if it's a holiday. 

Regarding strikes, that’s interesting. I just find it hard to understand the idea of joining strikes at all. In Germany, we strongly believe in finding other ways to address issues rather than resorting to that.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ahmed
shared_prefix.message:
I understand your point about May 1st being International Workers' Day, and that's definitely a significant day for discussions. But we can find a way to connect without the holiday, right? 

As for strikes, I think it's fascinating how we all approach issues differently. Deep down, we are all the same, just trying to express our concerns in ways that feel right to us. People are pretty much motivated by the same things—working together for a better outcome. I believe there are many ways to communicate and address concerns without strikes.
shared_prefix.label: Minimization
